A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SineProject and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original SineProject experiments on safety and privacy unlearning, along with ablations, geometric analyses, and human evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports a sigmoid modulation comparison in Table 6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the same frozen-projector parameterization W + sin(ΔW), trainable biases, and unlearning objectives. Sigmoid modulation is added as an ablation comparator, not as a component of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Safety and celebrity-privacy unlearning coverage is unchanged, as are the appendix evaluations of general vision-language capabilities, entangled concepts, high deletion ratios, and continual unlearning. The new benchmark-limitations discussion does not add evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds W + σ(ΔW), a sigmoid modulation comparator, to the existing regularization and bounded-function comparison. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The sigmoid comparison uses the retained SafeEraser/LLaVA-7B/PO+PD setting. No changes to existing splits, metrics, training budgets, model configurations, or testing procedures are reported; the layer-specific results referenced by the new freeze-ablation summary already appear in v1.

E4.justification: The function-selection ablation expands to test sigmoid alongside tanh, sine, and existing regularization alternatives. The layer-specific ablation in Table 7 and the remaining robustness, failure-mode, and human analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed main experiments, standard-deviation reporting, ten-seed initialization analysis, paired t-tests, Wilcoxon tests, and effect-size calculations are unchanged. The new limitations section repeats existing seed information.

E6.justification: v2 adds sigmoid results in Table 6, including SARR 32.3%, W2 Jacobian condition number 1.13×10^4, and MIR 4.75. Previously reported results remain unchanged, including baseline SARR 30.3% and SineProject SARR 25.8% in that comparison.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and the appendix Jacobian propositions, derivations, and proof are unchanged after matching Appendix B in v1 to Appendix C in v2. The sigmoid discussion adds interpretation rather than a formal theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about alignment drift, sinusoidal projector stabilization, forgetting–retention trade-offs, and negligible overhead. The added comparison supports existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix A discusses prompt sensitivity and the lack of large, semantically diverse forget sets. Appendix E.1 additionally attributes sigmoid's poorer refusal performance to its asymmetric positive bias. Existing architectural, semantic-entanglement, and certified-unlearning limitations remain.

D1.justification: The first-page footnote changes from promising code release upon acceptance to reporting code availability and providing a repository address. This establishes improved access information in the PDF, without independently verifying the repository. Existing implementation and hyperparameter specifications are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on parameter-efficient fine-tuning, conditioning and attention, and prompt-sensitive evaluation, including RandLoRA and EvoRefuse. Section 3.1 expands the conditioning discussion to pretraining and fine-tuning, while the broader related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short benchmark-limitations appendix and acknowledgments, updates the affiliation, and locally expands the conditioning and ablation discussion. Existing appendices are renumbered, but most wording and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 6 gains a sigmoid row, Table 2 is made more compact, and some tables and paragraphs move through reflow. The eight figures retain their visual content; there is no substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: The added sigmoid comparison modestly strengthens the evidence for choosing sinusoidal modulation, while explicit discussion of prompt sensitivity and dataset diversity clarifies evaluation limits. Code-access instructions also improve reproducibility information. These are targeted gains; the central method, theory, and previously reported results remain unchanged.
